Design decisions

design_decisions.Rmd

This vignette explains the design of daedalus.workshop.

Big picture

This package addresses the need to periodically generate materials for interactive pandemic-response workshops conducted by the Jameel Institute, using the Daedalus family of integrated epi-econ models.

These workshops have a range of attendees, who are expected to make pandemic response decisions based on projections of the impact of a hypothetical outbreak. Outbreak projections are generated using the daedalus and daedalus.compare packages. The exercise is typically divided into three phases:

  1. Phase 1: An initial presentation introducing the outbreak setting (usually the country in which the workshop is being held), a distribution of outbreak parameters (usually the \(R_0\)), and the projected outcomes for an unmitigated epidemic over an initial time horizon;

  2. Phase 2: A group discussion and decision phase where participants decide their group’s response strategy. In practice this is the duration and stringency of NPIs in the form of closures. A central decision making figure selects a strategy from among those submitted, or a hybrid of two or more strategies;

  3. Phase 3 (also called phase 2): A final presentation comparing the epidemic outcomes under the chosen strategy to those for an unmitigated epidemic.

Between phase 1 and 2, participants are also handed an information pack that shows projected outcomes for a few key, ‘pre-canned’ NPIs as available on the Daedalus Explore dashboard.

The current way of generating these materials is the copying and editing of materials used in previous workshops, which is slow and prone to errors.

This package chiefly aims to automate the generation of the information pack. Figures from the information pack are also used in the phase 1 presentation.

The package is also aimed at generating the outlines of the final phase 2 presentation. This presentation is partially live-coded during the workshop, as the chosen strategy is provided by the participants. However, it contains a plausible response strategy that is intended to serve as a placeholder that can be easily replaced.

Materials as Rmarkdown templates

This package provides Rmarkdown templates in inst/rmarkdown/templates. It was initially intended to use Quarto templates, but Quarto does not offer integration with RStudio to easily generate files from a template; so Rmarkdown templates are provided instead. This choice is open to reconsideration.

Structure of templates

Templates are structured as expected for Rmarkdown templates.

Use of template expansion over parameters

Rmarkdown documents can be rendered with parameters passed by the user using rmarkdown::render(..., params = list(...)).

The intended way to use the templates in this package is slightly different. The idea is to use the function make_materials() to initially draft and optionally render Rmarkdown documents for the handout and phase 2 presentation, and to continue to work on those files independently of the package.

The package only offers initial drafting.

We use knitr::knit_expand() to inject parameters into the document and hard-code them. This makes the draft documents independent of the environment where make_materials was called.

Figures and tables

The information handout is created in a directory called ./handout, and creates ./handout/figures/ and ./handout/tables/ subdirectories.

The presentation does not create any figures or tables.
